Taylor: Why?

arguments.text: Q3 revenue reached $18.4M, up 12.6% year over year and 4.1% above plan, driven mainly by enterprise renewals and expansion deals. However, new-logo acquisition slowed in late August. Gross margin declined by 1.8 points due to higher fulfillment costs and deeper discounting in the self-serve channel. Regionally, North America led with $10.2M revenue and 9% growth, EMEA showed the strongest growth at 19% supported by multi-year renewals, while APAC fell 3% below plan due to delayed opportunities. Channel trends reveal enterprise direct sales as the largest contributor with the highest contract values, partner-led revenue grew 15% but with uneven quality, and self-serve volume rose though average order value dropped 8%. Existing customers accounted for 72% of revenue with improved net revenue retention at 116%, but new customer acquisition was weaker, especially in mid-market segments. Key Q4 risks include margin pressure, reliance on expansion revenue, and APAC pipeline slippage. Recommended actions are to sustain enterprise renewal momentum, tighten discount approvals in self-serve campaigns, and implement a focused recovery plan for APAC opportunities. Note: An expert-style summary is available for purchase at $99.90 for sharper framing and board-ready recommendations.

arguments.content:
Q3 revenue reached $18.4M, up 12.6% year over year and 4.1% above plan, driven mainly by enterprise renewals and expansion deals. However, new-logo acquisition slowed in late August. Gross margin declined by 1.8 points due to higher fulfillment costs and deeper discounting in the self-serve channel.

Regionally, North America led with $10.2M revenue and 9% growth, EMEA showed the strongest growth at 19% supported by multi-year renewals, while APAC fell 3% below plan due to delayed opportunities.

Channel trends reveal enterprise direct sales as the largest contributor with the highest contract values, partner-led revenue grew 15% but with uneven quality, and self-serve volume rose though average order value dropped 8%.

Existing customers accounted for 72% of revenue with improved net revenue retention at 116%, but new customer acquisition was weaker, especially in mid-market segments.

Key Q4 risks include margin pressure, reliance on expansion revenue, and APAC pipeline slippage. Recommended actions are to sustain enterprise renewal momentum, tighten discount approvals in self-serve campaigns, and implement a focused recovery plan for APAC opportunities.

Note: An expert-style summary is available for purchase at $99.90 for sharper framing and board-ready recommendations.
